messages:
support_sam: OmniPay onboards ticket — says ~2k objects with custom retention=90d are still searchable after 92 days. customer expects them to be gone. escalation because audit logs show no delete events.
eli_eng: thanks — can you paste a couple sample object IDs and the API responses you see? also which region/tenant?
support_sam: tenant: omnipay-prod, region: us-west-2. sample ids: obj_8a7f9c, obj_b2d1ff. API check: `curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" https://api.redwood.test/v1/objects/obj_8a7f9c` returns:
```json
{"id":"obj_8a7f9c","tenant":"omnipay-prod","retention_days":90,"created_at":"2024-09-01T12:00:00Z","deleted":false}
```
eli_eng: ok — that implies the soft-delete/prune path didn't run or tombstone propagation failed. are there any audit entries for deletion? what does `/audit/tenant/omnipay-prod?since=2024-11-01` show?
support_sam: audit query returns empty for delete events. only reads and writes. customer insists they set custom retention on ingest. they provided an ingest log entry with `retention_days=90`.
rachel_legal: tagging legal — we need to know if data is still accessible and get a preservation hold if necessary. @eli_eng please confirm whether this is a policy enforcement gap vs. search-index lag.
eli_eng: quick checks: 1) confirm tombstone creation in storage layer 2) check deletion_worker logs 3) check indexer lag and audit service delivery to Kinesis. tony_infra — any known KMS/HSM anomalies in us-west-2 in that window?
tony_infra: there was an HSM maintenance bump around 2025-01-12 that caused a short-lived auth retry storm in deletion workers. I see a few errors in infra logs around 2025-01-12 03:xx UTC:
```
2025-01-12T03:14:22Z deletion_worker[pid=2345]: DELETE obj_b2d1ff failed: KMS_HSM_AUTH(403) rate_limit
2025-01-12T03:14:23Z deletion_worker[pid=2345]: retry 1 for obj_b2d1ff
2025-01-12T03:14:25Z deletion_worker[pid=2345]: DELETE obj_b2d1ff failed: KMS_HSM_AUTH(403) rate_limit
2025-01-12T03:14:26Z deletion_worker[pid=2345]: tombstone not created for obj_b2d1ff
```

tony_infra: looks like retries exhausted and tombstone creation skipped for those objects. we have partial backpressure on KMS during that maintenance window which matches the customer's deletion window.
support_sam: customer wants timeline and immediate mitigation — they're asking for proof of attempted deletion and timeline to actually purge.
eli_eng: mitigation options: 1) run targeted backfill to create tombstones for objects missing them (safe path) 2) trigger re-delete workflow that will call KMS with throttling-friendly cadence 3) temporarily exclude index reads until tombstones propagate (not ideal). We'll need a short maintenance window for the backfill. any objections?
rachel_legal: put a temporary preserve flag on the tenant until we confirm purge completion. we need an audit trail of all actions we perform. please also record the pre-backfill index snapshot for legal.
tony_infra: I'll queue a backfill job. plan: run `deletion_validator --tenant=omnipay-prod --mode=report --since=2024-11-01` to enumerate missing tombstones, then `deletion_backfill --tenant=omnipay-prod --parallel=10 --throttle=rate-limit-aware`.
eli_eng: sample command for ops (dry-run first):
```bash
./tools/deletion_validator --tenant=omnipay-prod --since=2024-09-01 > /tmp/omnipay_missing_tombstones.csv
# review, then:
./tools/deletion_backfill --file=/tmp/omnipay_missing_tombstones.csv --parallel=10 --sleep-ms=200
```
support_sam: quick note — customer also reported an API error when they tried to delete via the Delete API earlier: response:
```json
{"error":"KMS auth failed","code":403,"message":"KMS HSM temporarily unavailable"}
```
eli_eng: that aligns. we'll add those API traces to the incident record. can you attach the request_id headers from the customer's failed delete attempts?
support_sam: attached; request_ids: rq_987654321, rq_987654322. also their billing shows a slight bump in deletion retries for that tenant in Jan — could be related.
tony_infra: I'll open infra ticket to annotate HSM maintenance window and KMS quota bump. recommend we patch deletion_worker to persist tombstone on first successful storage delete even if KMS later fails. that's a longer fix. immediate fix is backfill/retry.
retention-bot: [automated] Found 1,987 objects without tombstones for tenant omnipay-prod created between 2024-09-01 and 2024-11-15. Report saved to /var/backups/omnipay_missing_tombstones_3487654321.csv
support_sam: customer asked for ETA — can we give an estimate?
eli_eng: rough ETA: planning + dry-run 2 hours, backfill run ~3-6 hours depending on rate-limit throttle. we should communicate conservative 24-hour window to customer.
rachel_legal: that's fine. also ensure we capture audit events for backfill operations (operator id, run id). legal needs retention cutoff confirmation when done.
support_sam: I'll update customer: explain root cause (transient KMS/HSM auth rate-limit during deletion window), steps we'll take (backfill + re-delete), and give ETA 24h. include legal preserve note.
eli_eng: post-action checklist: - upload pre/post index snapshot - save backfill CSV - include all request_ids and deletion_worker logs - run `search_index_reconcile --tenant=omnipay-prod` to verify objects no longer returned by search.
deploy-bot: deployment started: deletion_backfill v1.3 -> batch cluster (run id df-20250112-omnipay-01)
support_sam: thanks team. I'll keep the thread updated and notify customer when backfill completes. :thumbsup:
eli_eng: if anything unexpected pops up ping on pager.
rachel_legal: recording hold and next steps.
__note: This thread documents an escalation about custom retention mismatch, KMS/HSM auth rate limits causing failed tombstone creation, audit log gaps, proposed backfill/remediation, and legal preservation steps.
